title: Sell Mineral Rights in Connoquenessing, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Connoquenessing, PA | Butler Co
metaDescription: Connoquenessing sits in Butler County's layered legacy-gas and Marcellus territory. We buy PA mineral rights directly from owners, cash offer, no broker fees.
heroLead: Connoquenessing takes its name from the creek that winds through this part of Butler County, farmland that's carried gas leases, in one form or another, for well over a century.
intro: Butler County families near Connoquenessing often describe the same slow discovery: a small royalty check that's arrived for as long as anyone can remember, from a well nobody's actually seen, tied to a lease that predates everyone currently living. We hear that a lot in this part of the state, and it usually means you're sitting on a legacy shallow-gas interest that's been quietly producing for decades.

Whether your interest is that kind of legacy production or something tied to newer Marcellus development, we buy them both directly, in cash, without asking you to navigate a broker or a listing process.

sections.heading: Creek-Valley Farmland With a Long Gas History
paragraphs: The farmland around Connoquenessing sits in a part of Butler County where shallow gas wells were common well before Marcellus shale was ever a phrase anyone used. Those old wells were often drilled into formations a few thousand feet shallower than Marcellus, under leases that can still technically be active decades later, even producing small but steady royalty. Sorting out whether your family's lease covers just the shallow interval, or extends to depth, is central to knowing what you actually own.
We check that distinction carefully, since it changes both what's producing now and what could be leased separately in the future.

sections.heading: Small, Steady Checks and What They're Really Worth
paragraphs: A legacy shallow well can keep producing a modest royalty for decades without much drama, which is exactly why families tend to hold onto these interests indefinitely rather than considering a sale. But a small, steady check isn't the same as a valuable asset if the well is near the end of its productive life. We look at the well's actual production history before telling you what a lump-sum offer might make sense against.

sections.heading: One Deed, Multiple Heirs
paragraphs: Because these Connoquenessing-area leases are so old, ownership has often split several ways over multiple generations. If you're one of several cousins who each inherited a slice of a great-grandparent's interest, we can make an offer on your individual share without requiring every other heir to sell alongside you.

faqs.question: My royalty check comes from a well I've never seen. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Yes, especially for legacy shallow-gas interests around Connoquenessing. The wellsite doesn't have to be visible from your property to be part of your unit or lease.

faqs.question: Does my old lease cover Marcellus depth gas too, or just the shallow well?
faqs.answer: It depends on the specific lease language. Some older leases cover all depths, others are limited to the formation originally drilled. We check this before making an offer.

faqs.question: I only inherited a share of the family interest, not the whole thing. Can I still sell?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can buy your individual fractional share without requiring other heirs to sell theirs.
